as_told.title: Kona Blue failed special access program

plain: Kona Blue is said to be the name of a planned secret US government program about unidentified flying objects, whose existence came out when an internal slide presentation was made public. Jesse Michels brings it up in his own words while talking with a guest. He says it was "released I think by accident" and calls it "like a UAP program of some sort", UAP being the government's term for unidentified aerial phenomena. A fuller account comes from an online researcher who goes by UAPGerb, speaking without naming a source. He dates it to 2010 and calls it a "failed prospective special access program", meaning a proposed program with very tightly restricted access that never got started. He credits AARO, the Pentagon office that now studies unexplained aerial reports, with releasing the slide deck. He also names three people tied to it: Glenn Gaffney, Robert Cardio and Rob Jones. The tellers raise it because a proposal like that would show that people inside government once tried to set up a formal secret UFO effort.
